raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
Follow-up to #8791 (RFC #8790). The vocab-parallel logprobs / entropy / KL ops ran each row chunk as a dozen separate eager fp32 kernels. On the same local shard they were about 2–2.4× slower than a dense `log_softmax`, which offsets most of the memory benefit when they are used for OPSD / RL losses (e.g. deepspeedai/DeepSpeedExamples#1019).

## Changes
- New `deepspeed/ops/triton_ops/vocab_parallel_softmax.py`: Triton kernels with one program per row, looping over the local vocabulary in blocks. The module has no communication.
  - Local max and sum-exp are computed in a single read. They are then rescaled to the global max, so TP still needs only one MAX and one SUM all-reduce.
  - Fused forward and backward for entropy and KL, and a fused backward for logprobs (the top-k one-hot terms are added in fp32 before the single cast, as before).
- `deepspeed/sequence/vocab_parallel_ops.py` dispatches to these kernels on CUDA/XPU when the inputs are contiguous and `deepspeed.HAS_TRITON` is true. Otherwise it runs the existing eager path, which is unchanged. Collectives and the autograd structure are the same.
- Docs: a note in `autotp-training.md`.

## Performance
Intel Arc Pro B70, bf16, 75968-column shard (Qwen vocab / TP2), forward + backward:

| op | N | master | this PR | extra peak memory |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| reverse KL | 8192 | 340.8 ms | 15.5 ms | 510 MiB → ~0 |
| forward KL | 8192 | 313.0 ms | 15.5 ms | 446 MiB → ~0 |
| entropy | 8192 | 205.5 ms | 9.1 ms | 335 MiB → ~0 |
| logprobs (k=1) | 8192 | 99.5 ms | 7.2 ms | 192 MiB → ~0 |
| reverse KL | 2048 | 85.1 ms | 4.0 ms | |

- KL is within ~10% of the 608 GB/s memory-bandwidth floor.
- Logprobs with a large top-k is slower (k=256: 35 ms) but still about 3× faster than master.
- For reference, `torch.compile` of the eager chunk functions reached 26.9 ms for reverse KL (N=8192), so I chose hand-written kernels.

## Tests
- New `test_triton_kernels_match_eager_path` (fp32 / bf16 × logprobs / entropy / forward KL / reverse KL). On an accelerator it compares the Triton outputs and gradients with the CPU eager path. Cases: multiple kernel blocks, partially masked vocabulary, all-`-inf` rows, support mismatch with underflowing probability, large offsets, duplicate / ignored top-k ids, and a fully ignored row.
  - I checked that it fails when the kernel's support-mismatch `inf` is removed.
- The TP=2 tests (uneven and empty shards) now run through the Triton path.

Executed on 2× Intel Arc Pro B70 (XPU), torch 2.14.0.dev+xpu, Triton 3.8.0:
- `tests/unit/v1/sequence_parallelism/test_vocab_parallel_ops.py`: 41 passed.
- The existing single-process semantic tests, with XPU as the default device (so they run through Triton): 30 passed.


## Update: single-pass entropy/KL forward (by @0z5a)

The tables above were measured on the first commit. @0z5a's `e8038bed3` reads each logit once in the entropy/KL forward, using online weighted statistics. Both commits were re-measured with the same script on 1× B70: bf16, a 75968-column shard, forward + backward, median of 20 runs.

| op | N | `99f054192` | head `97d4f66df` |
|---|---|---|---|
| reverse KL | 8192 | 18.7 ms | 14.6 ms |
| forward KL | 8192 | 18.7 ms | 14.6 ms |
| entropy | 8192 | 9.2 ms | 7.1 ms |
| logprobs (k=1) | 8192 | 7.4 ms | 7.4 ms |
| reverse KL | 2048 | 4.8 ms | 3.9 ms |

Extra peak memory, excluding inputs and gradients, is below 1 MiB on both commits.

**Numerics vs the first commit.** Compared on 1× and 2× B70 (TP=1, TP=2), fp32 and bf16. Cases: 512×32000, 256×151936, and 64×32000 with a +1000 offset and `-inf` masks. Each output and gradient was also compared with an fp64 CPU reference.
- `logprobs`: outputs and gradients are bitwise identical.
- `entropy` / KL: not bitwise identical, because the summation order changed. Forward outputs differ by at most 35 ULP. The forward is closer to fp64 on almost every case: e.g. fp32 entropy relative error drops from 3e-7 to 1.5e-7, and KL from about 6–9e-7 to 3–8e-7. Gradient errors stay at the same level, and bf16 gradient errors are unchanged (about 2e-3).
- There are no `inf`/`NaN` placement differences.

## Contribution checklist

**Related work.** This is a performance follow-up to #8791 (RFC #8790). A search for vocab-parallel Triton kernels and entropy/KL found no overlapping PR.

**Commands and results.** Hardware and software: 2× Intel Arc Pro B70 (XPU, XCCL), Level Zero driver 1.15.39122 (compute runtime 26.27.39122.11), torch 2.14.0.dev20260804+xpu, Triton 3.8.0.
```
pytest -p no:randomly tests/unit/v1/sequence_parallelism/test_vocab_parallel_ops.py
```
At head `8f463213f`: 49 passed on 2× B70; with `DS_ACCELERATOR=cpu`, 33 passed and the 16 Triton tests are skipped.

**Compatibility matrix.**

| | Validated | Not validated |
|---|---|---|
| Precision | fp32, bf16 | fp16 |
| Parallelism | TP=1, TP=2 (uneven and empty shards) | TP>2 on device |
| Layout | Contiguous rows, plus `row_layout` strides from `e8038bed3` | |
| Accelerator | XPU (Triton); CUDA (Triton, 2× H100, validated by @0z5a); CPU (eager fallback, Triton tests skipped) | |

ZeRO and offload do not interact with these ops.

**AI assistance.** This PR was developed with AI assistance (GitHub Copilot CLI). I reviewed every changed line and ran the tests above.

Thanks for the Triton follow-up. I validated it on H100 and tried a few kernel-level changes on top of it; numbers and a patch are below.

### #8838 on H100

- `tests/unit/v1/sequence_parallelism/test_vocab_parallel_ops.py` on 2× H100 (CUDA path, including the TP=2 uneven and empty-shard tests): 41 passed. The single-process semantic tests with CUDA as the default device (so they run through Triton): 39 passed.
- torch 2.12.1+cu130, Triton 3.7.1, driver 595.91.07.
- The kernels are already at the memory-bandwidth floor for their pass count. For reverse KL with a detached teacher, fwd+bwd reads the student and teacher shards three times and writes one gradient (7 full passes). At the measured copy bandwidth that is about 5.9 ms for a bf16 8192 × 75968 shard, and the kernels take 5.83 ms.
- The default launch configuration is already the best on H100. In a sweep of BLOCK 1024–8192 × 4–32 warps, nothing was more than 1% faster than 4096 / 16; some settings were up to 9% slower.

### Suggested change: read each logit once in the entropy / KL forward

Since the kernels are bandwidth bound, the remaining lever is the number of passes. The forward currently reads each input twice: once for the local max and sum-exp, then again for the entropy or KL terms. The first pass can also accumulate the probability-weighted sum of logits centred on the running max: Σ e^(z−m)(z−m) for entropy, and Σ e^(a−m_a)((a−m_a)−(b−m_b)) for KL(A‖B). When the max grows, these sums are rescaled the same way as the sum-exp.

After the MAX all-reduce, each shard's sums are re-centred on the global max:

- H = log S − W / S
- KL = W / S_A − log S_A + log S_B

Centring on the max keeps a large common offset from cancelling in fp32; your large-offset test still passes. Support mismatch, meaning B masks a token that A supports, is a flag decided on the logits; it shares the MAX all-reduce. With TP the forward then needs one MAX and one SUM all-reduce instead of one MAX and two SUMs. The backward kernels are unchanged.

Separately, rows are addressed with up to two strides, so a slice such as `logits[:, :-1]` is read in place. Today `_flatten` copies such a slice with `reshape` in both forward and backward. Layouts the kernels cannot address, such as a strided vocabulary dimension, are still copied first, as before. Gradients are returned contiguous. I added one sentence about this to the tutorial note.

H100, fwd+bwd, 8192 × 75968 shard. The #8838 and patch columns are medians of 3 interleaved runs with nothing else on the node; the eager column comes from a single run.

| op | eager (#8791) | #8838 | #8838 + patch |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| reverse KL, bf16 | 133 ms | 5.83 ms | 4.48 ms |
| reverse KL, fp32 input | 117 ms | 11.5 ms | 8.39 ms |
| entropy, bf16 | 79.6 ms | 3.46 ms | 2.69 ms |
| logprobs k=1, bf16 | 37.7 ms | 2.80 ms | 2.82 ms |
| reverse KL, bf16 `logits[:, :-1]` | 141 ms | 13.6 ms (+2.3 GiB peak) | 4.47 ms (no extra peak) |

- The forward alone is 1.7× (bf16) to 1.9× (fp32) faster. fp32 reverse KL is at the 5-pass bandwidth floor.
- The single-pass statistics keep up to six running values per lane, so they use 2048-wide blocks. With 4096 they ran about 1.2× slower on H100.
- logprobs is unchanged: within 1% at 8192 rows, and about 25 µs slower at 1024 rows.
- At an OPSD chunk of 1024 rows, bf16 reverse KL is about the same (0.82 → 0.81 ms), and fp32 input is 1.27× faster.

All outputs and gradients match the eager path within your test tolerances, with NaN/inf in the same places. Validation:

- The full test file passes on 2× H100: 49 passed, including the new test. The new test covers a sequence slice and a strided vocabulary; positions outside the view hold NaN, so reading them would fail.
- The single-process semantic tests pass on CUDA with fp32 default tolerances: 47 passed.
- A CPU run under `TRITON_INTERPRET=1`, including gloo TP=2 with uneven and empty shards, matches the eager path.

One side effect I noticed, on a 1024 × 75968 KL in both directions: with the patch, bf16 and fp32 inputs give bitwise identical outputs, and the bf16 gradient equals the round-to-nearest-even of the fp32 one. With the current kernels they differ by up to 4e-6. My guess is that the per-thread layout, and so the reduction order, depends on the dtype; I have not verified that. Either way it is harmless, just a note.

I have not run anything on XPU, so the 2048-wide statistics blocks are only tuned on H100. I opened the patch as a single-commit PR against your branch: https://github.com/jinyouzhi/DeepSpeed/pull/5. Feel free to take all or part of it.

AI assistance was used for the implementation and analysis; I reviewed the changes and the measurements.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Guard zero rescaling before applying infinite shifts**

When a valid fp32/bfloat16 row spans the finite extremes (for example `[-3e38, 3e38]`), `row_max - run_max` overflows to `inf` while `scale` underflows to zero, so this evaluates `0 * (0 - inf)` and writes NaN into the weighted sum. The eager implementation returns entropy 0 for this one-hot distribution; the analogous updates in `_kl_stats_kernel` and the TP re-centering in `_triton_entropy`/`_triton_kl_div` have the same 0×inf or inf−inf failure, even yielding NaN for KL of two identical rows. Mask the weighted contribution when the rescale is zero, including in the distributed re-centering, before multiplying by the shift.

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# DeepSpeed Team
+"""Triton kernels for the vocabulary-parallel log-probability, entropy and KL ops.
+
+Each kernel handles one row of a ``[..., local_vocab]`` logits shard and loops over the local
+vocabulary in blocks, so no ``[rows, local_vocab]`` fp32 temporary is materialized. The kernels
+only see the local shard; ``deepspeed.sequence.vocab_parallel_ops`` owns the all-reduces and the
+autograd functions, and keeps an eager fallback with the same semantics.
+
+Rows are the flattened leading dimensions and are addressed in place (see ``row_layout``), so a
+slice such as ``logits[:, :-1]`` is read without first being copied into a ``[rows, vocab]`` view.
+Gradients are returned contiguous.
+
+``global_max`` and ``log_sum_exp`` are the global per-row softmax statistics, kept separate as in
+the eager path, and a log-probability is ``(z - global_max) - log_sum_exp``.
+
+The entropy and KL forward passes need one read of their inputs. Alongside each shard's max and
+sum-exp they accumulate a probability-weighted sum of logits centred on that max, which can be
+re-centred on the global max after the MAX all-reduce. Centring keeps a large common logit offset
+from cancelling in fp32, as in the eager path.
+"""
+
+import torch
+
+from deepspeed.ops.triton_ops._triton import _TRITON_AVAILABLE, triton, tl
+
+_MAX_BLOCK = 4096
+_NUM_WARPS = 16
+# The single-pass entropy and KL statistics keep up to six running values per lane; with a smaller
+# block they stay in registers (on H100 the KL statistics ran about 1.2x faster than with 4096).
+_STATS_MAX_BLOCK = 2048
+
+if _TRITON_AVAILABLE:
+
+    @triton.jit
+    def _row_start(row, inner_rows, outer_stride, row_stride):
+        return (row // inner_rows) * outer_stride + (row % inner_rows) * row_stride
+
+    @triton.jit
+    def _log_probs(ptr, cols, mask, global_max, log_sum_exp):
+        z = tl.load(ptr + cols, mask=mask, other=float("-inf")).to(tl.float32)
+        return (z - global_max) - log_sum_exp
+
+    @triton.jit
+    def _local_softmax_stats_kernel(x_ptr, max_ptr, sum_ptr, vocab, x_inner, x_outer, x_row, BLOCK: tl.constexpr):
+        # A single read computes the local max together with the sum-exp relative to it, by
+        # rescaling each lane's running sum whenever its running max grows.
+        row = tl.program_id(0).to(tl.int64)
+        x_ptr += _row_start(row, x_inner, x_outer, x_row)
+        lane_max = tl.full([BLOCK], float("-inf"), tl.float32)
+        lane_sum = tl.zeros([BLOCK], tl.float32)
+        for start in range(0, vocab, BLOCK):
+            cols = start + tl.arange(0, BLOCK)
+            z = tl.load(x_ptr + cols, mask=cols < vocab, other=float("-inf")).to(tl.float32)
+            new_max = tl.maximum(lane_max, z)
+            # exp(-inf - -inf) is NaN; a lane that has only seen -inf keeps a zero sum.
+            empty = new_max == float("-inf")
+            lane_sum = tl.where(empty, 0.0, lane_sum * tl.exp(lane_max - new_max) + tl.exp(z - new_max))
+            lane_max = new_max
+        row_max = tl.max(lane_max, axis=0)
+        row_sum = tl.sum(tl.where(lane_max == float("-inf"), 0.0, lane_sum * tl.exp(lane_max - row_max)), axis=0)
+        tl.store(max_ptr + row, row_max)
+        tl.store(sum_ptr + row, row_sum)
+
+    @triton.jit
+    def _entropy_stats_kernel(x_ptr, out_ptr, num_rows, vocab, x_inner, x_outer, x_row, BLOCK: tl.constexpr):
+        # Local max m, sum_j exp(z_j - m), and sum_j exp(z_j - m) * (z_j - m). Raising the max from m
+        # to m' scales both sums by exp(m - m') and shifts the centred logits by -(m' - m).
+        row = tl.program_id(0).to(tl.int64)
+        x_ptr += _row_start(row, x_inner, x_outer, x_row)
+        run_max = tl.full([BLOCK], float("-inf"), tl.float32)
+        run_sum = tl.zeros([BLOCK], tl.float32)
+        run_weighted = tl.zeros([BLOCK], tl.float32)
+        for start in range(0, vocab, BLOCK):
+            cols = start + tl.arange(0, BLOCK)
+            z = tl.load(x_ptr + cols, mask=cols < vocab, other=float("-inf")).to(tl.float32)
+            new_max = tl.maximum(run_max, z)
+            # Sums that have only seen -inf are still 0 and must stay finite.
+            seen = run_max != float("-inf")
+            scale = tl.where(seen, tl.exp(run_max - new_max), 0.0)
+            run_weighted = tl.where(seen, scale * (run_weighted - (new_max - run_max) * run_sum), 0.0)
+            run_sum = run_sum * scale
+            live = z != float("-inf")
+            e = tl.where(live, tl.exp(z - new_max), 0.0)
+            run_sum += e
+            run_weighted += tl.where(live, e * (z - new_max), 0.0)
+            run_max = new_max
+        # Re-centre every lane on the row max before summing the lanes.
+        row_max = tl.max(run_max, axis=0)
+        seen = run_max != float("-inf")
+        scale = tl.where(seen, tl.exp(run_max - row_max), 0.0)
+        run_weighted = tl.where(seen, scale * (run_weighted - (row_max - run_max) * run_sum), 0.0)

+            # Sums that have only seen -inf are still 0 and must stay finite.
+            seen = run_max != float("-inf")
+            scale = tl.where(seen, tl.exp(run_max - new_max), 0.0)
+            run_weighted = tl.where(seen, scale * (run_weighted - (new_max - run_max) * run_sum), 0.0)
+            run_sum = run_sum * scale
+            live = z != float("-inf")
+            e = tl.where(live, tl.exp(z - new_max), 0.0)
+            run_sum += e
+            run_weighted += tl.where(live, e * (z - new_max), 0.0)
+            run_max = new_max
+        # Re-centre every lane on the row max before summing the lanes.
+        row_max = tl.max(run_max, axis=0)
+        seen = run_max != float("-inf")
+        scale = tl.where(seen, tl.exp(run_max - row_max), 0.0)
+        run_weighted = tl.where(seen, scale * (run_weighted - (row_max - run_max) * run_sum), 0.0)

detail.body:
Follow-up to #8791 (RFC #8790). The vocab-parallel logprobs / entropy / KL ops ran each row chunk as a dozen separate eager fp32 kernels. On the same local shard they were about 2–2.4× slower than a dense `log_softmax`, which offsets most of the memory benefit when they are used for OPSD / RL losses (e.g. deepspeedai/DeepSpeedExamples#1019).

## Changes
- New `deepspeed/ops/triton_ops/vocab_parallel_softmax.py`: Triton kernels with one program per row, looping over the local vocabulary in blocks. The module has no communication.
  - Local max and sum-exp are computed in a single read. They are then rescaled to the global max, so TP still needs only one MAX and one SUM all-reduce.
  - Fused forward and backward for entropy and KL, and a fused backward for logprobs (the top-k one-hot terms are added in fp32 before the single cast, as before).
- `deepspeed/sequence/vocab_parallel_ops.py` dispatches to these kernels on CUDA/XPU when the inputs are contiguous and `deepspeed.HAS_TRITON` is true. Otherwise it runs the existing eager path, which is unchanged. Collectives and the autograd structure are the same.
- Docs: a note in `autotp-training.md`.

## Performance
Intel Arc Pro B70, bf16, 75968-column shard (Qwen vocab / TP2), forward + backward:

| op | N | master | this PR | extra peak memory |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| reverse KL | 8192 | 340.8 ms | 15.5 ms | 510 MiB → ~0 |
| forward KL | 8192 | 313.0 ms | 15.5 ms | 446 MiB → ~0 |
| entropy | 8192 | 205.5 ms | 9.1 ms | 335 MiB → ~0 |
| logprobs (k=1) | 8192 | 99.5 ms | 7.2 ms | 192 MiB → ~0 |
| reverse KL | 2048 | 85.1 ms | 4.0 ms | |

- KL is within ~10% of the 608 GB/s memory-bandwidth floor.
- Logprobs with a large top-k is slower (k=256: 35 ms) but still about 3× faster than master.
- For reference, `torch.compile` of the eager chunk functions reached 26.9 ms for reverse KL (N=8192), so I chose hand-written kernels.

## Tests
- New `test_triton_kernels_match_eager_path` (fp32 / bf16 × logprobs / entropy / forward KL / reverse KL). On an accelerator it compares the Triton outputs and gradients with the CPU eager path. Cases: multiple kernel blocks, partially masked vocabulary, all-`-inf` rows, support mismatch with underflowing probability, large offsets, duplicate / ignored top-k ids, and a fully ignored row.
  - I checked that it fails when the kernel's support-mismatch `inf` is removed.
- The TP=2 tests (uneven and empty shards) now run through the Triton path.

Executed on 2× Intel Arc Pro B70 (XPU), torch 2.14.0.dev+xpu, Triton 3.8.0:
- `tests/unit/v1/sequence_parallelism/test_vocab_parallel_ops.py`: 41 passed.
- The existing single-process semantic tests, with XPU as the default device (so they run through Triton): 30 passed.


## Update: single-pass entropy/KL forward (by @0z5a)

The tables above were measured on the first commit. @0z5a's `e8038bed3` reads each logit once in the entropy/KL forward, using online weighted statistics. Both commits were re-measured with the same script on 1× B70: bf16, a 75968-column shard, forward + backward, median of 20 runs.

| op | N | `99f054192` | head `97d4f66df` |
|---|---|---|---|
| reverse KL | 8192 | 18.7 ms | 14.6 ms |
| forward KL | 8192 | 18.7 ms | 14.6 ms |
| entropy | 8192 | 9.2 ms | 7.1 ms |
| logprobs (k=1) | 8192 | 7.4 ms | 7.4 ms |
| reverse KL | 2048 | 4.8 ms | 3.9 ms |

Extra peak memory, excluding inputs and gradients, is below 1 MiB on both commits.

**Numerics vs the first commit.** Compared on 1× and 2× B70 (TP=1, TP=2), fp32 and bf16. Cases: 512×32000, 256×151936, and 64×32000 with a +1000 offset and `-inf` masks. Each output and gradient was also compared with an fp64 CPU reference.
- `logprobs`: outputs and gradients are bitwise identical.
- `entropy` / KL: not bitwise identical, because the summation order changed. Forward outputs differ by at most 35 ULP. The forward is closer to fp64 on almost every case: e.g. fp32 entropy relative error drops from 3e-7 to 1.5e-7, and KL from about 6–9e-7 to 3–8e-7. Gradient errors stay at the same level, and bf16 gradient errors are unchanged (about 2e-3).
- There are no `inf`/`NaN` placement differences.

## Contribution checklist

**Related work.** This is a performance follow-up to #8791 (RFC #8790). A search for vocab-parallel Triton kernels and entropy/KL found no overlapping PR.

**Commands and results.** Hardware and software: 2× Intel Arc Pro B70 (XPU, XCCL), Level Zero driver 1.15.39122 (compute runtime 26.27.39122.11), torch 2.14.0.dev20260804+xpu, Triton 3.8.0.
```
pytest -p no:randomly tests/unit/v1/sequence_parallelism/test_vocab_parallel_ops.py
```
At head `8f463213f`: 49 passed on 2× B70; with `DS_ACCELERATOR=cpu`, 33 passed and the 16 Triton tests are skipped.

**Compatibility matrix.**

| | Validated | Not validated |
|---|---|---|
| Precision | fp32, bf16 | fp16 |
| Parallelism | TP=1, TP=2 (uneven and empty shards) | TP>2 on device |
| Layout | Contiguous rows, plus `row_layout` strides from `e8038bed3` | |
| Accelerator | XPU (Triton); CUDA (Triton, 2× H100, validated by @0z5a); CPU (eager fallback, Triton tests skipped) | |

ZeRO and offload do not interact with these ops.

@@ -0,0 +1,366 @@
+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# DeepSpeed Team
+"""Triton kernels for the vocabulary-parallel log-probability, entropy and KL ops.
+
+Each kernel handles one row of a ``[..., local_vocab]`` logits shard and loops over the local
+vocabulary in blocks, so no ``[rows, local_vocab]`` fp32 temporary is materialized. The kernels
+only see the local shard; ``deepspeed.sequence.vocab_parallel_ops`` owns the all-reduces and the
+autograd functions, and keeps an eager fallback with the same semantics.
+
+Rows are the flattened leading dimensions and are addressed in place (see ``row_layout``), so a
+slice such as ``logits[:, :-1]`` is read without first being copied into a ``[rows, vocab]`` view.
+Gradients are returned contiguous.
+
+``global_max`` and ``log_sum_exp`` are the global per-row softmax statistics, kept separate as in
+the eager path, and a log-probability is ``(z - global_max) - log_sum_exp``.
+
+The entropy and KL forward passes need one read of their inputs. Alongside each shard's max and
+sum-exp they accumulate a probability-weighted sum of logits centred on that max, which can be
+re-centred on the global max after the MAX all-reduce. Centring keeps a large common logit offset
+from cancelling in fp32, as in the eager path.
+"""
+
+import torch
+
+from deepspeed.ops.triton_ops._triton import _TRITON_AVAILABLE, triton, tl
+
+_MAX_BLOCK = 4096
+_NUM_WARPS = 16
+# The single-pass entropy and KL statistics keep up to six running values per lane; with a smaller
+# block they stay in registers (on H100 the KL statistics ran about 1.2x faster than with 4096).
+_STATS_MAX_BLOCK = 2048
+
+if _TRITON_AVAILABLE:
+
+    @triton.jit
+    def _row_start(row, inner_rows, outer_stride, row_stride):
+        return (row // inner_rows) * outer_stride + (row % inner_rows) * row_stride
+
+    @triton.jit
+    def _log_probs(ptr, cols, mask, global_max, log_sum_exp):
+        z = tl.load(ptr + cols, mask=mask, other=float("-inf")).to(tl.float32)
+        return (z - global_max) - log_sum_exp
+
+    @triton.jit
+    def _local_softmax_stats_kernel(x_ptr, max_ptr, sum_ptr, vocab, x_inner, x_outer, x_row, BLOCK: tl.constexpr):
+        # A single read computes the local max together with the sum-exp relative to it, by
+        # rescaling each lane's running sum whenever its running max grows.
+        row = tl.program_id(0).to(tl.int64)
+        x_ptr += _row_start(row, x_inner, x_outer, x_row)
+        lane_max = tl.full([BLOCK], float("-inf"), tl.float32)
+        lane_sum = tl.zeros([BLOCK], tl.float32)
+        for start in range(0, vocab, BLOCK):
+            cols = start + tl.arange(0, BLOCK)
+            z = tl.load(x_ptr + cols, mask=cols < vocab, other=float("-inf")).to(tl.float32)
+            new_max = tl.maximum(lane_max, z)
+            # exp(-inf - -inf) is NaN; a lane that has only seen -inf keeps a zero sum.
+            empty = new_max == float("-inf")
+            lane_sum = tl.where(empty, 0.0, lane_sum * tl.exp(lane_max - new_max) + tl.exp(z - new_max))
+            lane_max = new_max
+        row_max = tl.max(lane_max, axis=0)
+        row_sum = tl.sum(tl.where(lane_max == float("-inf"), 0.0, lane_sum * tl.exp(lane_max - row_max)), axis=0)
+        tl.store(max_ptr + row, row_max)
+        tl.store(sum_ptr + row, row_sum)
+
+    @triton.jit
+    def _entropy_stats_kernel(x_ptr, out_ptr, num_rows, vocab, x_inner, x_outer, x_row, BLOCK: tl.constexpr):
+        # Local max m, sum_j exp(z_j - m), and sum_j exp(z_j - m) * (z_j - m). Raising the max from m
+        # to m' scales both sums by exp(m - m') and shifts the centred logits by -(m' - m).
+        row = tl.program_id(0).to(tl.int64)
+        x_ptr += _row_start(row, x_inner, x_outer, x_row)
+        run_max = tl.full([BLOCK], float("-inf"), tl.float32)
+        run_sum = tl.zeros([BLOCK], tl.float32)
+        run_weighted = tl.zeros([BLOCK], tl.float32)
+        for start in range(0, vocab, BLOCK):
+            cols = start + tl.arange(0, BLOCK)
+            z = tl.load(x_ptr + cols, mask=cols < vocab, other=float("-inf")).to(tl.float32)
+            new_max = tl.maximum(run_max, z)
+            # Sums that have only seen -inf are still 0 and must stay finite. A scale that underflows to 0
+            # may come with an infinite shift when the maxima are finite extremes, so 0 * inf is skipped.
+            seen = run_max != float("-inf")
+            scale = tl.where(seen, tl.exp(run_max - new_max), 0.0)
+            run_weighted = tl.where(scale > 0, scale * (run_weighted - (new_max - run_max) * run_sum), 0.0)
+            run_sum = run_sum * scale
+            live = z != float("-inf")
+            e = tl.where(live, tl.exp(z - new_max), 0.0)
+            run_sum += e
+            run_weighted += tl.where(e > 0, e * (z - new_max), 0.0)
+            run_max = new_max
+        # Re-centre every lane on the row max before summing the lanes.
+        row_max = tl.max(run_max, axis=0)
+        seen = run_max != float("-inf")
+        scale = tl.where(seen, tl.exp(run_max - row_max), 0.0)
+        run_weighted = tl.where(scale > 0, scale * (run_weighted - (row_max - run_max) * run_sum), 0.0)
+        run_sum = run_sum * scale
+        tl.store(out_ptr + row, row_max)
+        tl.store(out_ptr + num_rows + row, tl.sum(run_sum, axis=0))
+        tl.store(out_ptr + 2 * num_rows + row, tl.sum(run_weighted, axis=0))
+
+    @triton.jit
+    def _entropy_backward_kernel(x_ptr, max_ptr, lse_ptr, entropy_ptr, grad_out_ptr, grad_ptr, vocab, x_inner, x_outer,
+                                 x_row, BLOCK: tl.constexpr):
+        # dH / dz_j = -p_j * (log p_j + H)
+        row = tl.program_id(0).to(tl.int64)
+        x_ptr += _row_start(row, x_inner, x_outer, x_row)
+        grad_ptr += row * vocab
+        global_max = tl.load(max_ptr + row)
+        log_sum_exp = tl.load(lse_ptr + row)
+        entropy = tl.load(entropy_ptr + row)
+        grad_out = tl.load(grad_out_ptr + row)
+        undefined_row = global_max == float("-inf")
+        for start in range(0, vocab, BLOCK):
+            cols = start + tl.arange(0, BLOCK)
+            mask = cols < vocab
+            log_p = _log_probs(x_ptr, cols, mask, global_max, log_sum_exp)
+            grad = tl.where(log_p == float("-inf"), 0.0, tl.exp(log_p) * (log_p + entropy)) * -grad_out
+            grad = tl.where(undefined_row, 0.0, grad)
+            tl.store(grad_ptr + cols, grad.to(grad_ptr.dtype.element_ty), mask=mask)
+
+    @triton.jit
+    def _logprobs_backward_kernel(x_ptr, max_ptr, lse_ptr, grad_sum_ptr, zero_row_ptr, index_ptr, index_grad_ptr,
+                                  grad_ptr, vocab, x_inner, x_outer, x_row, num_index, BLOCK: tl.constexpr):
+        # d logp(i) / d z_j = onehot(i)_j - softmax(z)_j, summed over the requested indices.
+        row = tl.program_id(0).to(tl.int64)
+        x_ptr += _row_start(row, x_inner, x_outer, x_row)
+        grad_ptr += row * vocab
+        index_ptr += row * num_index
+        index_grad_ptr += row * num_index
+        global_max = tl.load(max_ptr + row)
+        log_sum_exp = tl.load(lse_ptr + row)
+        grad_sum = tl.load(grad_sum_ptr + row)
+        zero_row = tl.load(zero_row_ptr + row) != 0
+        for start in range(0, vocab, BLOCK):
+            cols = start + tl.arange(0, BLOCK)
+            mask = cols < vocab
+            log_p = _log_probs(x_ptr, cols, mask, global_max, log_sum_exp)
+            grad = tl.where(zero_row, 0.0, tl.exp(log_p) * -grad_sum)
+            # The one-hot terms are added in fp32 before the single cast, as in the eager path.
+            for k in range(0, num_index):
+                local_index = tl.load(index_ptr + k)
+                if (local_index >= start) & (local_index < start + BLOCK):
+                    grad += tl.where(cols == local_index, tl.load(index_grad_ptr + k), 0.0)
+            tl.store(grad_ptr + cols, grad.to(grad_ptr.dtype.element_ty), mask=mask)
+
+    @triton.jit
+    def _kl_stats_kernel(a_ptr, b_ptr, out_ptr, num_rows, vocab, a_inner, a_outer, a_row, b_inner, b_outer, b_row,
+                         BLOCK: tl.constexpr):
+        # For KL(A || B) over the local shard: both maxima and sum-exps, whether A has support that
+        # B masks out, and sum_j exp(a_j - m_a) * ((a_j - m_a) - (b_j - m_b)). Raising the maxima
+        # scales that sum by exp(m_a - m_a') and shifts the centred log-ratio by -(dm_a - dm_b).
+        row = tl.program_id(0).to(tl.int64)
+        a_ptr += _row_start(row, a_inner, a_outer, a_row)
+        b_ptr += _row_start(row, b_inner, b_outer, b_row)
+        a_max = tl.full([BLOCK], float("-inf"), tl.float32)
+        b_max = tl.full([BLOCK], float("-inf"), tl.float32)
+        a_sum = tl.zeros([BLOCK], tl.float32)
+        b_sum = tl.zeros([BLOCK], tl.float32)
+        weighted = tl.zeros([BLOCK], tl.float32)
+        mismatch = tl.zeros([BLOCK], tl.int32)
+        for start in range(0, vocab, BLOCK):
+            cols = start + tl.arange(0, BLOCK)
+            mask = cols < vocab
+            za = tl.load(a_ptr + cols, mask=mask, other=float("-inf")).to(tl.float32)
+            zb = tl.load(b_ptr + cols, mask=mask, other=float("-inf")).to(tl.float32)
+            new_a_max = tl.maximum(a_max, za)
+            new_b_max = tl.maximum(b_max, zb)
+            a_seen = a_max != float("-inf")
+            b_seen = b_max != float("-inf")
+            a_scale = tl.where(a_seen, tl.exp(a_max - new_a_max), 0.0)
+            b_scale = tl.where(b_seen, tl.exp(b_max - new_b_max), 0.0)
+            # A sum that has seen A but no finite B holds only mismatched terms, which the final
+            # +inf replaces, so dropping it keeps the -inf shift from producing NaN.
+            shift = (new_a_max - a_max) - (new_b_max - b_max)
+            weighted = tl.where(b_seen & (a_scale > 0), a_scale * (weighted - shift * a_sum), 0.0)
+            a_sum = a_sum * a_scale
+            b_sum = b_sum * b_scale
+            a_live = za != float("-inf")
+            b_live = zb != float("-inf")
+            ea = tl.where(a_live, tl.exp(za - new_a_max), 0.0)
+            a_sum += ea
+            b_sum += tl.where(b_live, tl.exp(zb - new_b_max), 0.0)
+            # Tokens A masks out contribute nothing; where B masks out a token A supports, KL(A || B) is
+            # infinite even if p_A underflows to 0, so this is decided on the logits.
+            weighted += tl.where(b_live & (ea > 0), ea * ((za - new_a_max) - (zb - new_b_max)), 0.0)
+            mismatch |= (a_live & ~b_live).to(tl.int32)
+            a_max = new_a_max
+            b_max = new_b_max
+        # Re-centre every lane on the row maxima before summing the lanes.
+        row_a_max = tl.max(a_max, axis=0)
+        row_b_max = tl.max(b_max, axis=0)
+        a_seen = a_max != float("-inf")
+        b_seen = b_max != float("-inf")
+        a_scale = tl.where(a_seen, tl.exp(a_max - row_a_max), 0.0)
+        b_scale = tl.where(b_seen, tl.exp(b_max - row_b_max), 0.0)
+        shift = (row_a_max - a_max) - (row_b_max - b_max)
+        weighted = tl.where(b_seen & (a_scale > 0), a_scale * (weighted - shift * a_sum), 0.0)
+        a_sum = a_sum * a_scale
+        b_sum = b_sum * b_scale
+        tl.store(out_ptr + row, row_a_max)
+        tl.store(out_ptr + num_rows + row, row_b_max)
+        tl.store(out_ptr + 2 * num_rows + row, tl.max(mismatch, axis=0).to(tl.float32))
+        tl.store(out_ptr + 3 * num_rows + row, tl.sum(a_sum, axis=0))
+        tl.store(out_ptr + 4 * num_rows + row, tl.sum(b_sum, axis=0))
+        tl.store(out_ptr + 5 * num_rows + row, tl.sum(weighted, axis=0))
+
+    @triton.jit
+    def _kl_backward_kernel(a_ptr, b_ptr, a_max_ptr, a_lse_ptr, b_max_ptr, b_lse_ptr, kl_ptr, grad_out_ptr, a_grad_ptr,
+                            b_grad_ptr, vocab, a_inner, a_outer, a_row, b_inner, b_outer, b_row,
+                            NEED_A_GRAD: tl.constexpr, NEED_B_GRAD: tl.constexpr, BLOCK: tl.constexpr):
+        # For KL(A || B): dKL/dz_A = p_A * (log p_A - log p_B - KL) and dKL/dz_B = p_B - p_A.
+        row = tl.program_id(0).to(tl.int64)
+        a_ptr += _row_start(row, a_inner, a_outer, a_row)
+        b_ptr += _row_start(row, b_inner, b_outer, b_row)
+        a_grad_ptr += row * vocab
+        b_grad_ptr += row * vocab
+        a_max = tl.load(a_max_ptr + row)
+        a_lse = tl.load(a_lse_ptr + row)
+        b_max = tl.load(b_max_ptr + row)
+        b_lse = tl.load(b_lse_ptr + row)
+        kl = tl.load(kl_ptr + row)
+        grad_out = tl.load(grad_out_ptr + row)
+        # KL is undefined when either distribution is; both sides then get zero gradient.
+        undefined_row = (a_max == float("-inf")) | (b_max == float("-inf"))
+        for start in range(0, vocab, BLOCK):
+            cols = start + tl.arange(0, BLOCK)
+            mask = cols < vocab
+            a_log_p = _log_probs(a_ptr, cols, mask, a_max, a_lse)
+            b_log_p = _log_probs(b_ptr, cols, mask, b_max, b_lse)
+            a_p = tl.exp(a_log_p)
+            if NEED_A_GRAD:
+                a_grad = tl.where(a_log_p == float("-inf"), 0.0, a_p * (a_log_p - b_log_p - kl)) * grad_out
+                a_grad = tl.where(undefined_row, 0.0, a_grad)
+                tl.store(a_grad_ptr + cols, a_grad.to(a_grad_ptr.dtype.element_ty), mask=mask)
+            if NEED_B_GRAD:
+                b_grad = tl.where(undefined_row, 0.0, (tl.exp(b_log_p) - a_p) * grad_out)
+                tl.store(b_grad_ptr + cols, b_grad.to(b_grad_ptr.dtype.element_ty), mask=mask)
+
+
+def row_layout(logits):
+    """``(inner_rows, outer_stride, row_stride)`` addressing every row of ``logits`` in place, or None.
+
+    Two levels of row strides cover contiguous tensors and slices along a sequence dimension such
+    as ``logits[:, :-1]``, which cannot be viewed as ``[rows, vocab]`` without a copy.
+    """
+    if logits.shape[-1] > 1 and logits.stride(-1) != 1:
+        return None
+    sizes, strides = [], []
+    for size, stride in zip(logits.shape[:-1], logits.stride()[:-1]):
+        if size == 1:
+            continue
+        if sizes and strides[-1] == stride * size:
+            sizes[-1] *= size
+            strides[-1] = stride
+        else:
+            sizes.append(size)
+            strides.append(stride)
+    if len(sizes) > 2:
+        return None
+    sizes = [1] * (2 - len(sizes)) + sizes
+    strides = [0] * (2 - len(strides)) + strides
+    return sizes[1], strides[0], strides[1]
+
+
+def _num_rows(logits):
+    return logits.shape[:-1].numel()
+
+
+def _launch(kernel, logits, *args, max_block=None, **kwargs):
+    # An empty local shard still launches: the loops run zero times and the statistics kernels write -inf and 0.
+    if _num_rows(logits) == 0:
+        return
+    vocab = logits.shape[-1]
+    block = min(max_block or _MAX_BLOCK, max(16, triton.next_power_of_2(vocab)))
+    kernel[(_num_rows(logits), )](*args, **kwargs, BLOCK=block, num_warps=_NUM_WARPS)
+

Thanks for the Triton follow-up. I validated it on H100 and tried a few kernel-level changes on top of it; numbers and a patch are below.

### #8838 on H100

- `tests/unit/v1/sequence_parallelism/test_vocab_parallel_ops.py` on 2× H100 (CUDA path, including the TP=2 uneven and empty-shard tests): 41 passed. The single-process semantic tests with CUDA as the default device (so they run through Triton): 39 passed.
- torch 2.12.1+cu130, Triton 3.7.1, driver 595.91.07.
- The kernels are already at the memory-bandwidth floor for their pass count. For reverse KL with a detached teacher, fwd+bwd reads the student and teacher shards three times and writes one gradient (7 full passes). At the measured copy bandwidth that is about 5.9 ms for a bf16 8192 × 75968 shard, and the kernels take 5.83 ms.
- The default launch configuration is already the best on H100. In a sweep of BLOCK 1024–8192 × 4–32 warps, nothing was more than 1% faster than 4096 / 16; some settings were up to 9% slower.

### Suggested change: read each logit once in the entropy / KL forward

Since the kernels are bandwidth bound, the remaining lever is the number of passes. The forward currently reads each input twice: once for the local max and sum-exp, then again for the entropy or KL terms. The first pass can also accumulate the probability-weighted sum of logits centred on the running max: Σ e^(z−m)(z−m) for entropy, and Σ e^(a−m_a)((a−m_a)−(b−m_b)) for KL(A‖B). When the max grows, these sums are rescaled the same way as the sum-exp.

After the MAX all-reduce, each shard's sums are re-centred on the global max:

- H = log S − W / S
- KL = W / S_A − log S_A + log S_B

Centring on the max keeps a large common offset from cancelling in fp32; your large-offset test still passes. Support mismatch, meaning B masks a token that A supports, is a flag decided on the logits; it shares the MAX all-reduce. With TP the forward then needs one MAX and one SUM all-reduce instead of one MAX and two SUMs. The backward kernels are unchanged.

Separately, rows are addressed with up to two strides, so a slice such as `logits[:, :-1]` is read in place. Today `_flatten` copies such a slice with `reshape` in both forward and backward. Layouts the kernels cannot address, such as a strided vocabulary dimension, are still copied first, as before. Gradients are returned contiguous. I added one sentence about this to the tutorial note.
